_comment: tmux-shaped hotkeys for Superset -- managed in dotfiles, applied with
`superset-tmux-keys apply`. Superset has no prefix key: bindings are single
chords matched by react-hotkeys-hook, so ctrl+alt stands in for tmux's C-b.
It is the only modifier space that is free of macOS (cmd is not: cmd+h/x/z/c
are Hide/Cut/Undo/Copy), free of the PTY (Superset forwards plain ctrl to the
terminal and reserves ctrl+C/D/Z/S/Q/backslash), and free of Superset's own
defaults (which are all cmd-based plus ctrl+1..9 for presets).
tmux's shifted punctuation is bound to the same physical key without shift,
so the fingers land where they already do: " -> ctrl+alt+quote,
matches the printed key rather than the scan code, which is what Superset
uses for its own printable defaults.
